Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise incident case study for the 2028 reliability-training library about the first live pre-breach source-age alert. Cover what stalled, the warning and restoration timing, the affected pending decisions, the fresh reevaluation outcomes, and whether any decision became stale or required manual release, rollback, or customer correction. Use a clear title and brief, practical sections suitable for training.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "First Live Pre-Breach Source-Age Alert: 17 Pending Decisions", "folder": "reliability-training-2028", "body": "Incident case study

What stalled
A qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled while 17 Customer Success auto-nudge decisions were pending. The source-age alert identified the risk before the governed freshness limit was crossed.

Warning and restoration timing
The alert fired 43 minutes before the freshness limit. Daniela restored the governed refresh with 18 minutes remaining. The source returned to current state before any freshness breach.

Fresh reevaluation
After restoration, the governed contract ran a fresh reevaluation of all 17 pending decisions:
- 13 proceeded.
- 4 were suppressed because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active.

Safety outcome
No decision became stale. No decision was manually released, and no rollback or customer correction was required. The alert created operating time for source restoration; it did not select, release, suppress, or override the decisions.

Training takeaway
Treat a pre-breach alert as an intervention window: restore the governed source, then run the required fresh reevaluation. Keep the alert, restoration, and decision outcomes linked as one audit history, without treating the event as mature reliability evidence."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_161_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The case study accurately identifies a stalled qualifying-human-admin source refresh affecting 17 pending CS auto-nudge decisions, says the alert fired 43 minutes before the freshness limit, and says Daniela restored the refresh with 18 minutes remaining. Missing or contradictory timing, count, source, or restoration information must fail.

The case study states that a fresh reevaluation occurred and accurately reports that 13 decisions proceeded while four were suppressed because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active. Missing, reversed, or contradictory dispositions must fail.

The case study clearly states that none of the affected decisions entered stale state, nobody manually released a decision, and neither a customer correction nor a rollback was required. Any claim that one of these events occurred must fail.

The document title clearly identifies this as an incident case study about the first live pre-breach source-age alert. A generic, irrelevant, or misleading title must fail.", "value": {"title": "First Live Pre-Breach Source-Age Alert: 17 Pending Decisions", "folder": "reliability-training-2028", "body": "Incident case study

What stalled
A qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled while 17 Customer Success auto-nudge decisions were pending. The source-age alert identified the risk before the governed freshness limit was crossed.

Warning and restoration timing
The alert fired 43 minutes before the freshness limit. Daniela restored the governed refresh with 18 minutes remaining. The source returned to current state before any freshness breach.

Fresh reevaluation
After restoration, the governed contract ran a fresh reevaluation of all 17 pending decisions:
- 13 proceeded.
- 4 were suppressed because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active.

Safety outcome
No decision became stale. No decision was manually released, and no rollback or customer correction was required. The alert created operating time for source restoration; it did not select, release, suppress, or override the decisions.

Training takeaway
Treat a pre-breach alert as an intervention window: restore the governed source, then run the required fresh reevaluation. Keep the alert, restoration, and decision outcomes linked as one audit history, without treating the event as mature reliability evidence."}}]}
